slides.title: VoiceGuard: An Audio-Native LLM-VLA Pipeline for Wheelchair-Mounted Assistive Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work integrates audio-native LLMs and vision-language-action policies to enable natural language control of wheelchair-mounted robotic arms, addressing challenges in intent validation, interruption handling, and execution reliability for assistive manipulation.

card.one_liner: VoiceGuard uses audio-native LLMs and local validation to enable safe, voice-controlled wheelchair-mounted robotic manipulation.
card.key_idea: Separates spoken intent from execution via on-device stop detectors, structured packet validation, and SmolVLA policies for task-level control.
card.evaluation: Preliminary tests on a prototype showed 55/60 correct routing, 16/20 deliveries, and 20/20 stops with 210ms latency.
card.limitation: Evaluated only by lab members on fixed setups; lacks user studies and suffers from VLA robustness issues regarding lighting.

slides.title: TipDex-VTLA: Learning When to Refine Actions with Touch for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.tldr: TOUCH-GUIDED ACTION REFINEMENT FOR ROBUST MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work addresses action drift in dexterous manipulation caused by illumination changes by integrating visual reliability estimation with tactile forecast verification. It demonstrates that gating feature corrections based on tactile discrepancies significantly improves success rates under challenging, unseen lighting conditions.

card.one_liner: TipDex-VTLA uses visual reliability and tactile forecasts to refine actions under changing illumination.
card.key_idea: Combines Visual Action Sensitivity Estimation (VASE) and Tactile Anticipation/Correction (TACE) to gate bounded feature corrections for unexecuted actions.
card.evaluation: Tested on four real-world tasks and UniVTAC; achieves 73.8% success under unseen lighting, outperforming baselines like T-Rex and N0-VTLA.
card.limitation: Reliability estimation is a policy-dependent proxy learned solely from illumination perturbations, potentially limiting generalization to other visual disturbances.

slides.title: TacInno: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models the Contact Dynamics Beyond Vision and Action
slides.highlight: This work introduces a method to isolate unpredictable contact dynamics from visual and action cues, using them as a discrete training target to significantly improve Vision-Language-Action model performance in contact-rich manipulation.

card.one_liner: TacInno isolates unpredictable tactile dynamics as a training target, significantly boosting VLA performance in contact-rich tasks.
card.key_idea: A conditional tokenizer encodes tactile innovation into discrete codes, which the policy predicts as an auxiliary loss to refine tactile representations.
card.evaluation: Tested on six UniVTAC simulation tasks and four real-world tasks, outperforming baselines by ~10% and validating tactile reliance via ablations.
card.limitation: Requires pre-computing codes from demonstrations; extending the innovation concept to other modalities remains future work.

slides.title: CoRA-VTLA: Contact-Guided Attention and Queryable Response Memory for Tactile Post-Training
slides.highlight: This work introduces CoRA-VTLA, a method to augment pretrained vision-language-action models with tactile feedback using queryable response memory and contact-guided attention, improving precision manipulation success rates.

card.one_liner: CoRA-VTLA enhances pretrained VLAs for precision manipulation using contact-guided attention and queryable action-response memory.
card.key_idea: Augments VLAs with a queryable memory retrieving recent contact responses and gaze supervision grounding tactile tokens in visual contact regions.
card.evaluation: Tested on MuJoCo, UniVTAC, and real robots; achieves 73.33% mean success vs 50% for direct fusion, with statistically significant gains.
card.limitation: Requires synchronized tactile-visual demonstrations for post-training; safety during recovery and extended memory horizons remain open challenges.

slides.title: 3DTouch: A Tactile-aware VLA Model with 3D Geometric Relations for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a tactile-geometric conditioning approach for Vision-Language-Action models that integrates 3D scene geometry with spatially localized tactile feedback to improve contact-rich dexterous manipulation. By explicitly modeling hand-object and object-object relations, the method achieves significant success rate improvements over standard VLA baselines in real-world tasks.

card.one_liner: 3DTouch boosts dexterous manipulation success by grounding tactile forces in 3D space and modeling geometric relations.
card.key_idea: Encodes RGB-D points and taxel forces in a shared robot-base frame, plus explicit hand-object relations, to condition VLA policies.
card.evaluation: Tested on 5 real-world tasks with UR7e/XHand; 65% avg success, +20pp over Tactile-VLA, validated via ablations and pose robustness.
card.limitation: Relies on accurate 3D object pose estimation and reference meshes, limiting generalization to novel or occluded objects.

slides.title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
slides.tldr: PHYSICALLY GROUNDED EXECUTION FOR HUMANOID LOCO-MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This paper introduces PGX, a framework that decomposes long-horizon humanoid loco-manipulation into a state machine, VLA skills, and world-coordinate locking, demonstrating improved task success on a Unitree G1 robot.

card.one_liner: PGX improves long-horizon humanoid loco-manipulation by offloading timing and spatial precision to classical, training-free components.
card.key_idea: Decouples execution into a predicate-gated state machine for timing, VLA skills for manipulation, and world-coordinate locking for spatial consistency.
card.evaluation: Tested on three simulated tasks and one real Unitree G1 task using π0.5 and GR00T N1.6 backbones, showing significant success rate improvements.
card.limitation: Higher success rates come at the cost of longer execution times due to stage transitions and recovery mechanisms.

slides.title: PhyDEX: A Benchmark for Physical Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models via Dynamic Extrinsic Dexterity
slides.highlight: PhyDEX evaluates whether Vision-Language-Action models truly understand physics, such as mass and friction, by testing dynamic extrinsic dexterity tasks like throwing. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied learning, as it highlights the gap between current VLA capabilities and the physical reasoning required for robust human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: PhyDEX benchmarks VLA physical reasoning via throwing tasks, revealing current models fail to infer object dynamics.
card.key_idea: A synthetic benchmark using 35K trajectories of throwing tasks with randomized mass, center of mass, and friction to test physical inference.
card.evaluation: Evaluated GR00T, DynamicVLA, and ForceVLA on simulation, humanoid, and real-world setups; all achieved <3% success rates.
card.limitation: Focuses solely on throwing with simplified physics; current policies fail primarily due to pre-throw grasping errors and physical blindness.

slides.title: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models to Stop Safely
slides.tldr: SAFI enables safe mid-execution stopping for VLA models
slides.highlight: This work introduces State-Aware Fallback Imitation (SAFI) to ensure Vision-Language-Action models stop safely during execution, preventing physical incidents like dropped objects while preserving other skills.

card.one_liner: SAFI enables VLAs to safely stop prohibited tasks mid-execution by learning explicit holding fallbacks.
card.key_idea: Two-stage framework: constructs stationary holding targets for prohibited tasks, then jointly optimizes fallback and retained-task imitation.
card.evaluation: Tested on OpenVLA-OFT with LIBERO/BadLIBERO; achieved 1.3% prohibited success with zero physical incidents while preserving skills.
card.limitation: Currently limited to tasks where holding is a safe fallback; requires further validation on physical robots and diverse architectures.
